context_interested_parties.title: Proposed interested parties
context_interested_parties.intro: Interested parties are the people and organisations that affect your business or are affected by it: customers, employees, owners, suppliers, authorities and so on. For each one you note what they need and expect from you, and how you follow it up.
context_interested_parties.promptBody: We can propose the interested parties that are typical for a business like yours, with their needs and expectations, based on your company profile and what you already have registered.

context_swot.title: Proposed SWOT analysis
context_swot.intro: A SWOT analysis is a simple way to describe your situation: strengths and weaknesses inside the business, opportunities and threats outside it. It helps you see what the management system must take care of.
context_swot.promptBody: We can draft a first SWOT analysis for your business, based on your company profile and what you already have registered.

context_scopes.title: Proposed scope
context_scopes.intro: The scope says what your management system covers: which activities, sites and services are included, where the boundaries are, and which requirements of a standard do not apply to you (with a reason).
context_scopes.promptBody: We can propose a scope for each standard you work with, based on your company profile, sites and processes.

context_responsibilities.title: Proposed roles and responsibilities
context_responsibilities.intro: Here you decide who does what in the management system. For each task, RACI shows who does the work (R), who is accountable (A, always exactly one), who is consulted (C) and who is kept informed (I). In a small company one person often holds several roles.
context_responsibilities.promptTitle: Shall I propose roles and responsibilities for you?
context_responsibilities.promptBody: We propose the usual responsibilities for the standards you work with, using your own people, roles and departments, and link them to your processes where they exist.
